correctness.rationale: For half-angle α=γ/2 and nonzero mean direction m, write the two unit Bloch vectors as cos(α)m ± sin(α)e, with e perpendicular to m (arbitrary there if γ=0). The mean has length cos(α). For a unit transverse n, factorization gives zero cross covariance and variance [1−sin²(α)(e·n)²]/2. Its global minimum is cos²(α)/2, attained at n=e; at γ=0 all transverse axes tie. Both normalizations give the stated values, and taking γ→π gives an infimum but not a value at the undefined endpoint. The review's explicit product uses opposite transverse components ±√3/2 and common longitudinal component 1/2; the dot product is −1/2 and the variance minimum is 1/8. This exact witness is in the 2011 review, not the qualitative product paragraph of the 2003 preprint; correct the attribution when citing the example. The analytic minimization, not the recorded numerical output, supports the result.
